comments.text:
In Australia we run dedicated lines for urban passanger rail, state/interstate/regional passenger rail, and freight rail. If I want to get around Melbourne I use the Melbourne ptv metro lines. If I want to travel to another Victorian metro area, upstate, or interstate to Sydney, I can catch the metro to Southern Cross station and either catch a country link train running between the state capitals or a vline Victorian state train up just over the border and transfer over to nsw state rail. 

The capital stations that connect metro, state, and interstate also have separate freight sections. Southern Cross station connects freight from the docklands, port Melbourne, Melbourne's industrial district, out into the state, and interstate. You can see the freight infrastructure but it doesn't run on the same rails as the passenger trains. 

I believe the government owns all the freight rail but not the freight trains that run on it. If a business wants a rail connected to the network, they pay for and maintain their direct connection link and then negotiate their allowed throughput with the state/national rail provider. It works exactly the same as the National broadband network, but instead of data throughput and fibre optic cables, it's train cars and railways.

comments.text: 13:04 BRO what im going to say is not about amtrak but, in my town Ive grown up in there is a railroad that cuts through the whole town splitting the entire place in half through multiple train-car road intersections. Sometimes when theres a train going through one intersection if you are fast enough you can get to another crossing before it gets there 😂. Okay BUT Im pretty sure I have seen a direct effect of this statement as our town is lowkey SUFFERING from freight train... idiocy or lunacy idk what else to call it. The problem is no longer the trains rolling through and building up traffic on major roads as cars wait to get to where theyre going. It used to only take at most 10 min of waiting. NOW, it has become mind-boggling often that you wait for the train, you start to realize the train is slowing down.... The train comes to a complete stop RIGHT when you can see the end of the train in sight! But it is unable to pass the crossing!! And then! A 2nd train passes through!! So now you have to wait for double!! In many areas of the town there is a divider between the oncoming traffic way at train tracks, and because of this there is no way out in the car. One time I waited literally 40 minutes :( So it definitely appears like, the trains are too long for their own infrastructure now, that they cant pass the crossings before needing to stop to let another train pass. Its always like they stop and block the crossing when theres only 3 traincars still needing to cross... and then you just wait for like 10 minutes with 0 progress before the 2nd train pulls through... Anyway Im all for passenger rail and I love my car but hate car dependent infrastucture! Normalize passenger trains please!! Then we wouldnt have to deal with any of these delays in our "freedom" cars. Thankfully this year we have our very first overpass that goes over the train, it does not connect easily to the rest of the town but at least its an option finally.
